rome02_republic_domestic_1.where: Rome; the earlier Casa di Livia is the named same-city comparison
rome02_republic_domestic_1.when: Late Republic, first century BCE; not for the 509 BCE city
rome02_republic_domestic_1.basis: research/rome02_republic_forms.md H1; sources R20. Unchanged approved subura_domus_1 geometry. DAR describes an earlier one-storey Casa di Livia phase, perhaps75-50BCE. This is one generic residential court, not that named house or its roof reconstruction. Whole-house symmetry,3.5m/storey,court fraction.28,25deg roof,.35m eaves and closed ground are inherited massing estimates. No local frequency. Quarter placement and counts: research/rome02_republic_quarter_sources.md, not an excavated local census.

rome02_republic_domestic_2.where: Rome; generic court form and separately attested Republican upstairs lodging
rome02_republic_domestic_2.when: Late Republic; Plutarch describes earlier Republican life retrospectively
rome02_republic_domestic_2.basis: research/rome02_republic_forms.md H2; sources R20/R23/R24. Unchanged approved subura_domus_2 geometry, with period evidence replaced. Plutarch Sulla1.4 describes upper and lower rented accommodation in one house, not its total floors, courtyard, height or address. A complete uniformly two-level court is a schematic combination of the court comparison and this minimum vertical distinction.3.5m/storey,court.28, 25deg roof,.35m eaves and closed ground remain inherited estimates. No Hadrianic Ostia,Severan FUR or Augustan Livia addition is used as a Republican floor census. Not a two-storey maximum or named Sulla house. Quarter placement and counts: research/rome02_republic_quarter_sources.md, not an excavated local census.

rome02_republic_shop_range_1.basis: research/rome02_republic_forms.md H3; sources R01/R09/R19. Republican shop rows and adjoining passages are sourced; roof height,plot size and the single simplified range are comparative estimates. This is not a surveyed Tabernae Veteres unit, not a separate tenant per doorway, and does not establish that all commercial buildings were one-storey.
